headline: Five majors above their 200-day lines, but the crowd's Greed sits on top of red screens and exchange-bound coins
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is the most orderly part of today's tape. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses confirmed; DOGE and ADA sit below theirs with no golden cross. That is not a market of one story, it is two: a majority of large-caps in an established uptrend structure, and a couple of laggards that never repaired theirs. BTC itself is 38.2% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, which is a useful reminder that 'above the 200-day' and 'near the highs' are different claims entirely.

Layer on momentum and you find a mild but consistent divergence. Every asset in the set is negative on RSI-side neutral ground (BTC 54.4, ETH 59.5, SOL 54.8, XRP 51.5, BNB 55.5, DOGE 49.7, ADA 50.4) and every single one shows MACD below signal. Meanwhile daily changes are red across the board (BTC -0.2%, ETH -1.5%, SOL -1.3%, XRP -1.4%, BNB -1.4%, DOGE -1.4%, ADA -0.5%) and the weekly changes are redder still (BTC -5.1%, XRP -7.2%, ADA -6.7%, DOGE -4.8%, SOL -3.4%, BNB -1.1%, ETH -0.8%). Zoom out to 30 days and the picture flips entirely positive, with every asset up between 18% and 40%. Three windows, three different stories: the month says trend up, the week says pullback, the day says drift lower. That is a market resting inside a longer advance, not one breaking down, but the MACD-below-signal reading across all seven names says the resting phase has some momentum drag behind it worth watching rather than ignoring.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding on OKX runs at 0.0095% per 8 hours (10.4% annualized), a modest positive cost for longs to carry the position, against $2.17B in open interest and a long/short account ratio of 1.7, meaning retail accounts skew long even as price cools. ETH funding is negative (-1.9% annualized), a rare case where shorts are paying longs to hold the trade, alongside $1.62B of open interest. DOGE's long/short ratio of 4.56 and XRP's 2.92 show retail leaning hard into longs on the smaller names too, and DOGE liquidations lean lopsided at $517K longs versus just $6.9K shorts over 11 hours, a sign those long bets are getting tested. None of this is expensive-and-crowded in the way a blow-off top usually looks, but it is not flat and cheap either; funding and OI together describe a market with real leveraged length still in the boat.

The flow picture is where the real tension sits. BTC spot ETFs printed a net outflow of $13.2M on 11 Sep 2026, the fourth straight day in the same direction, adding up to a five-session net outflow of $288.1M. ETH ETFs did the opposite: a net inflow of $216.4M on 11 Sep 2026 and $222.8M over five sessions, though same_direction_days of 1 means that ETH inflow is a single-day event, not yet a run. Underneath both, whale wallets moved $173.4M net onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, with $164.9M of BTC specifically flowing into Coinbase against $77.3M and $57.6M flowing back off Coinbase in two separate moves, a genuine two-way tug rather than one-directional dumping. Zooming to the weekly cadence, three of the last four tracked weeks (ending Aug 23, Aug 30, and Sep 13) show net movement onto exchanges, with only the week ending Sep 06 showing net outflow off exchanges. Stablecoin float is up 1.35% over 30 days to $310.2B, so the dry powder is growing even as coins trend toward exchange balances, a combination that reads more like positioning for volatility than a one-sided verdict.

Sentiment sits at 61, labeled Greed, inside a 30-day range of 31 to 74, so the crowd is comfortably warm but nowhere near its own recent extreme. That is worth sitting with against a tape where BTC is down on the day and week, ETF flows for bitcoin have been net negative four sessions running, and whale coins are net moving toward exchanges more weeks than not. The gauge says the crowd feels good; the flow data says money has been leaving the BTC ETF wrapper and gravitating toward exchange wallets. When the mood and the money disagree this plainly, that gap is the story, not a footnote to it.

What to watch from here: whether BTC ETF flows turn positive and break the four-day outflow streak, whether ETH's single day of ETF inflow gets a second day to become a real trend, whether the long/short ratios on BTC (1.7) and DOGE (4.56) start to unwind as MACD stays below signal, and whether the weekly whale flow reading for the week ending Sep 20 repeats the 'onto exchanges' pattern seen in three of the last four weeks or breaks it like the week ending Sep 06 did.
